proposed text: 14.1 Data readiness — mandatory

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: Maintain a readiness record for each insight (detection rule, financial figure, market figure and any later insight) and project. It states the insight's state from its own gate (eligible, qualified, blocked or unavailable) and, for each input, how far it has reached: capture available, validation available, authority established, reconciliation available, decision-eligible. An insight is never shown as eligible while an input it needs is missing, unverified, conflicting, stale or not authoritative.

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: For each gap, record the entity and field, the period, the source, the reason (missing, unverified, conflicting, stale, not authoritative, or the underlying record does not exist), the likely holder, the action owner, the approver where one is needed, and the way in that supplies it, saying plainly when that way in is not built.

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: Give each gap a stable identity (entity, field, period and source) and a lifecycle: open, assigned, awaiting evidence, resolved, suppressed, reopened, superseded. A gap found again updates its existing record and nudge; suppression windows and re-notification rules follow Section 06 §9.1.

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: Reassess readiness at setup, after each intake batch or material change of state, on a schedule, and whenever a record is corrected, quarantined, superseded or revoked. Raise a shared missing setting once, with the projects it affects.

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: An insight may set a tighter freshness limit than its source's default for the inputs it depends on; an overall fresh status never hides a stale critical input. Starting thresholds are owner-approved parameters, each with a documented owner and rationale (Section 16 §5), reviewed in the pilot.

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: Show gaps with their factors side by side, as Section 10 §4 requires for findings: the amount affected, urgency, confidence in that amount, whether the person can act now, and what depends on it. A gap is never called a loss or confirmed leakage; any amount comes from a traceable Section 05 calculation or is labelled an estimate.

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: 14.2 Telling the builder what is needed — mandatory

which reads: Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
proposed text: Whenever a rule, figure or other insight cannot fully do a check or produce a figure, it must say so: what is missing, why it matters, what is to be done and by whom. No case may be silent, and nothing may be shown as complete when it is not. Each such message is proven by a test when it is built. A list of the messages, generated by scanning the code, is kept as a controlled artefact and fails when the code gives a message it does not cover.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: 18.1 Ways of supplying data — mandatory

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Every fact a person or system supplies, through any way in (import file, document or email, entry screen, setup question, site capture, integration), enters through the intake this section defines, with the same envelope (organisation, project, channel, the person or system, and the time) and the same control checkpoints; nothing writes a supplied fact to the store directly. Records Profit Guardian calculates are written by their calculation runs, with the run recorded (Section 03 §14.3).

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Every entity in the controlled entity register has at least one Level 1 way in that needs no particular builder software: an import template, document or email capture, an entry screen, a setup question, or a record Profit Guardian calculates. Site capture (Level 2) and integrations (Level 3) reduce effort; neither is ever the only way in.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Adding a way in, or a builder changing systems, may change the intake; it must not change any detection rule or financial figure, its logic or its test results. Teaching a rule or figure to use data it does not read today is a change to that rule under its own change request. Where two ways in supply the same field, the Source Authority Register decides which governs, never the most recent arrival.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: A way in that is not built is never offered to the builder as available.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: For each kind of record, name its supplier, checker, corrector, approver and the owner accountable if it stays missing; one person may hold several of these roles, and they stay distinct in the record.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: 18.2 Channel controls — mandatory

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Email capture verifies the sender and never takes the organisation from the address alone; a verified sender does not make a document genuine or authorised (§5 and §12 still apply). Original messages and attachments are kept.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Every uploaded file, attachment and photo is scanned and parsed in isolation within size, archive and resource limits before it is read; a malformed or unsupported file is rejected with a reason.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Entry screens and setup questions carry the signed-in person, pass the same validation as an imported row, and need approval where the register requires. They never edit a held record: correcting a quarantined or pending record goes through the review workflow (§9, §13).

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Where a person keys a material value from a document, a second person with the verifier role confirms it before it counts. Each value keeps its own confirmation and provenance, also when confirmation is done in batches.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Site capture devices are enrolled to the organisation; on a shared device the signed-in user is recorded; the time is checked against the server; each record says how its place was established. Site capture's privacy requirements follow Section 09 §14 and are settled before it is built.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: A record entered after the event it describes is marked retrospective. A backdated entry never rewrites a result already shown: the earlier result and the records it used stay on record, and the affected insight is reassessed and labelled.

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: 18.3 Setup questions — mandatory

which reads: Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
proposed text: Policies, maps, rates and settings the builder sets (the source registry, the Source Authority Register, the cost-code map, users and roles where the platform does not supply them, the financial policy with its status maps, and the rule settings) are supplied through setup questions, versioned, submitted through the intake, and take effect only after approval by the required role. Onboarding asks only what the insights the builder switches on need. A record whose cost code is not mapped yet completes intake and is held only from the figures that need the code.

Shown by a test.

proposed text: No manual way in (templates, documents, entry screens, site capture, setup answers) bypasses validation, approval or audit (§18). Setup answers are versioned and take effect only after approval by the required role.

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: Every uploaded file, email attachment and photo is scanned and parsed in isolation within size, archive and resource limits before it is read; a malformed or unsupported file is rejected with a reason.

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: A held record is corrected only through the review queue, never by an entry form.

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: The readiness record is reassessed at setup, after each intake batch or material state change, on its schedule, and when a record is corrected, quarantined, superseded or revoked; an insight is never shown as eligible while an input it needs is missing, unverified or stale.

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: Each data gap has a stable identity (entity, field, period, source) and moves through open, assigned, awaiting evidence, resolved, suppressed, reopened and superseded; a gap found again updates its existing nudge instead of creating a new one; suppression windows and re-notification rules are defined and tested (Section 06 §9.1).

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: A way in that is not built is never offered to the builder as available.

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: Every field a current rule or figure reads, including setting fields, has at least one built way in that carries it, with its authority and verification requirement met; and each way in, when built, carries every field of the entities it serves. Shown by a generated field-coverage report that fails on a gap; a first-release gate.

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: A partly failed or failed intake (a batch with rejected rows, an unreadable document, a stopped feed, an unmatched record) is shown as such, with its count and reasons, and never as a successful intake.

which reads: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live im
proposed text: Whenever a rule or figure cannot fully do a check or a figure, it says so: what is missing, why it matters and what the builder is to do. No case is silent, and nothing is shown as complete when it is not. Each message is proven by a test when it is built; a list generated by scanning the code holds every message the scan finds and fails if the code gives one it does not cover.

which reads: Do not claim an integration, security control or acceptance criterion passed without reproducible evidence.
proposed text: Bring every record kind under this section's intake, including the kinds checked today only inside the calculations and the records written straight to the store; take a regression baseline of today's rule and figure results first, explain and sign off every difference, and do it under its own change request.

which reads: Do not claim an integration, security control or acceptance criterion passed without reproducible evidence.
proposed text: Keep the controlled data-supply registers (entity, field, rule input contracts, field coverage, supply routes, messages) current, and regenerate the field-coverage report for each way in as it is built; the report fails on a gap.

which reads: A commitment is not automatically an additional cost on top of a forecast; determine whether it is already rep
proposed text: Present the authoritative figure first. Beside it, show each item that is not final in its own category (awaiting approval, on hold, disputed, rejected) with its amount and the effect it would have if it went through. These effects are labelled what-if amounts, are never added into the authoritative figure, and are isolated as Section 10 §7.1 requires.

which reads: Keep unresolved differences visible; do not force them into a clean-looking total.
proposed text: Where a cost is attributed to an instruction or variation, it stays in actual cost or commitments exactly once; the attribution groups it and never adds it a second time. A cost not attributed stays with the original scope.

which reads: Each rule requires a stable identifier, version, purpose, inputs, evaluation logic, thresholds, exceptions, se
proposed text: Rule thresholds and windows ship with defaults approved by the product owner; the builder's authorised approver accepts them at onboarding and may adjust them within the approved ranges. A setting with no sensible default (the builder's own categories, or pairs a person declares) is supplied by the builder when the rule is switched on.

which reads: Keep severity, urgency and confidence separate. A high-severity finding with weak evidence warrants careful ve
proposed text: The levels at which findings are graded by severity are set by the builder at setup: for each grade an amount, a percentage of the job, or both; with both set, the grade applies as soon as either is reached. The percentage is of the current approved contract value (original contract value plus approved variations) [owner to confirm]. No default or suggested levels are supplied. The levels are approved as other settings are (Section 04 §18.3) [approval route: owner decision]. Until they are set and approved, findings still show, marked ungraded, with what to do.

which reads: Disputed/rejected amount: Value subject to dispute, rejection or unresolved review.
proposed text: For a rejected variation, the builder records its outcome: disputed, carried at the builder's own cost, resubmitted, or withdrawn. Profit Guardian records that outcome and does not judge the dispute (§11); the cost already incurred stays visible.

proposed text: 8.2 Extras and variations view — mandatory

which reads: Potential, estimated, submitted, approved/certified, recognised, invoiced and collected values must remain dis
proposed text: Show the original contract scope's budget and profit on their own, and each extra or variation separately: its value in each state, its status, the cost incurred against it so far and its effect on the job's profit. The two are never blended, and no state is added into another.
